text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- For the first time a majority -- of 49.5 percent -- of Austrians see more advantages in the introduction of the European single currency euro than disadvantages.

- Civil servants in the finance ministry will hold a demonstration on June 26 in protest against job and pay cuts after two strikes failed to yield results. Chancellor Viktor Klima and Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel have signalled willigness for talks on the government's planned austerity measures.
- Klima and Schuessel say reports on planned reforms of the pension system are still being negotiated within the Social Affairs Ministry and are not yet ready for the government to discuss.
- The government plans to privatise the Austrian federal printer through the stock exchange as Print Media Austria.
- IFE will pay out an unchanged dividend of 20 schillings even though the company reported pre-tax losses of 15.9 million schillings.
- A 62-year old man was released after being held for two weeks in police custody on suspicion of penning two letters that claimed responsibility for 20 letterbombs.
- Experts say the early retirement age must rise significantly in order for the pension system to remain financially viable.
- Connect Austria is taking legal action against the Transport Ministry for extending the deadline for offers for the country's third mobil phone network licence.
- The government could receive up to 3.5 billion schillings from the introduction of a road-pricing system for trucks on Austria's motorways.
- The European Union authorized subsidies by Austria for German car manufacturer BMW's motor production facility in Upper Austria worth 345.7 million schillings.
- According to an OECD report Austria's deficit is expected to rise to 3.4 percent of GDP in 1998, after narrowly fulfilling the Maastricht criterium of 3.0 percent this year.
- Doubts are being raised over the efficiency of Social Affairs Minister Lore Hostasch's plans to reform the public pension system.
- Chamber of Economy expert Guenter Stummvoll says wage increases could be used to fund new pensions. However labour union representative Richard Leutner vehmently opposes the plan.

- Creditanstalt's Investmentbank reached a new record in in the first quarter with pre-tax profit jumping to 227.5 million schillings from 52.1 million. Creditanstalt Investmentbank head Alarich Fenyves says the investment bank's merger with Investmentbank Austria is "very likely".
